reason: Attacked and not broken. I pulled the Ellis scan myself (archive.org earlydiaryfranc01burngoog, the Google scan of the Cornell/Bell copy) and read the opening of the Juvenile Journal as searchable text. The wording stands letter for letter as proposed: 'To have some account of my thoughts, manners, acquaintance and actions, when the hour arrives in which time is more nimble than memory, is the reason which induces me to keep a Journal. A Journal in which I must confess my every thought, must open my whole heart!' The OCR carries a stray caret for the comma after 'thoughts' and a space before the exclamation mark, both typesetting artifacts, not different words. Every discriminating reading the verifier named holds: 'and' not an ampersand, 'in which the hour arrives' reads 'in which time is more nimble than memory' with 'in which' and not 'at which', a full stop after the first 'Journal', and 'my every thought'. The next words on the page are 'But a thing of this kind ought to be addressed to somebody', so the quotation ends at a real sentence break and mints nothing. Locator: the heading above it reads 'FRANCES BURNEY. / JUVENILE JOURNAL / Addressed to a Certain Miss Nobody. / Poland Street, London, March 27.' under the running head 'The Early Diary of [1768', and the only matter before it in the volume is Ellis's editorial introduction, so 'the first entry' is right and 27 March 1768 is right. The verifier was also right to drop the page: the running head OCRs as '4i' and cannot be read with confidence. Edition: the title page of the same scan reads 'EDITED BY ANNIE RAINE ELLIS ... IN TWO VOLUMES. VOL. I. LONDON: GEORGE BELL AND SONS, YORK STREET, COVENT GARDEN. 1889.', so editor, publisher, year and volume are all confirmed from the book itself and not from a secondary citation. Attribution is not in dispute and the line is on no misattribution list. Scope: a named work by a named author, first published 1889, not scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business or oratory. shipped.js returns shipped [], near [], yearCount 0 for 'frances burney', not banned, not at cap, and Burney appears in no other month 6 lane, so there is no in-month collision. Mechanics: the source line leads with the name, carries no dash, contains no straight double quote and runs 126 characters, inside the 140 cap; the quotation ends in an exclamation mark, uses no straight quotes and is prose that is not broken into lines. The tag Diary is the form of the work. Publishable, and a fifteen year old setting her own terms for honest writing is squarely the month's theme. The one soft spot worth naming, and it is not a refutation: the note field is empty, so nothing on the card tells a reader that Ellis's text is a different rendering from the 'at which time' version that circulates from Diary and Letters of Madame d'Arblay. An editor may want a one-line note saying the wording is Ellis's.
